title: Round 8 Gate B: steady-camera numbers (head / reflex / trunk / ORACLE / electronic / phase-locked)
written: 2026-11-05 15:39 CST -- before any measurement run (only the dev runs below had run)
question: How steady can the duck's camera view get, cheapest options first? Decides whether stage 2 (chicken head) is worth building and which kind (R8_STAGED_PLAN.md s3, s5 row B).
body: frozen M0 body (room.FROZEN_BODY, duck.py default actuator='xml'), frozen walker, frozen interface; MuJoCo 3.16.0

streams.head: head camera as now: 128 px, 45 deg, rendered exactly like Duck.head_image (sensor-only: it is the sensor)
streams.reflex: head camera with the gaze.py reflex on (paired physics run; scripted: m3_gaze's loop; bot: params {'gaze': True})
streams.trunk: SIM-ONLY hardware alternative: camera fixed to trunk_base at [0.05, 0.0, 0.02] m (front-top, ~0.14 m above the floor), tilted 10 deg down in the trunk frame, 45 deg, 128 px
streams.oracle: ORACLE (simulator truth): true head-camera position; orientation = the true head-camera orientation through the frozen target filter (yaw, pitch smoothed; roll held at 0 = level horizon); rendered directly, 45 deg, 128 px
streams.eis: electronic stabilisation, sensor-only: 140 deg render at 864 px from the head camera; orientation estimate from gyro (yaw integrated as odometry.py), the gravity reading (tilt) and the joint encoders through BodyModel.fk (the bot's camera model), read at 50 Hz; target = the estimate through the same frozen filter, roll 0; warp H = K R K^-1 (bilinear, numpy/scipy), crop to 45 deg / 128 px; the target is pulled toward the source axis when it is more than 39.54 deg away (then 100% of output pixels are inside the render)
streams.eis_lag: eis with the estimate and target from one 50 Hz sample earlier (a 20 ms sensor-to-frame latency); robustness row
streams.eis_lagc: eis_lag with the late estimate extrapolated one sample at its last rotation rate (constant-rate latency compensation); robustness row
streams.eis_reflex / eis_reflex_lag / eis_reflex: the eis warps applied on the reflex run (both at once)
streams.pl_head / pl_eis: phase-locked sampling of head / eis: the 50 Hz frame at each left-foot touchdown while walking (1 per stride, ~1.86 Hz). Gait phase from encoders + gravity only: the stance foot is the lower foot in the gravity-aligned trunk frame (odometry.py's rule) with a 2 mm hysteresis

frozen_parameters.filter_name: ma2: two cascaded moving averages of 27 samples (one stride at 1.86 Hz, 50 Hz) on yaw and pitch, no ramp term; delay 0.52 s
frozen_parameters.render: default room visuals (shadows, reflections, headlight) for every stream; separate MjData synced from the live one (qpos -> mj_kinematics -> mj_camlight)

dev_tuning.what: orientation-only runs (no renders); filter candidates ema tau 1.0/0.5 s, alpha-beta wn 1/2/4 rad/s, notch(ma2) with/without ramp terms, ma1; source FOV 100/120/140 deg
dev_tuning.rule: lowest mean of eis walking wobble yaw/2.0 and pitch/1.0 over the dev scripted walking average and the dev bot episodes
dev_tuning.result: ma2 at 140 deg: dev eis scripted walking 1.02/0.51 deg, dev bot 0.85/0.46 deg, clamp active 2.7% of scripted walking samples (100 deg: 28%)

scripted.head_command: (0, 0, 0, 0) + reflex offsets in the reflex run (m3_gaze.run)
scripted.note: same configs and segments as M3.1's validation (m3_gaze.py); reflex off and on

bot.rule: the first 10 train configs from index 40 whose set_lamp episode k=8 needs a press (r7_gaze_pregate's rule)
bot.controller: the frozen reference bot (refbot.controller), reflex off and on

episodes.pool: splits/train.json only (no dev, test, R7 or confirmation rooms); dev tuning rooms disjoint from both measurement sets

metrics.wobble: per stream, the effective view orientation (yaw/pitch of the forward axis, roll of the right axis vs horizontal) minus its centred 1 s moving mean, std in deg. Scripted: m3_gaze.detrended_std on 50 Hz steps 150..500 (M3.1's number). Bot: the whole episode detrended, std over walking steps (executed vx > 0.15). eis effective orientation = R_true_head * R_est^T * R_target (scored by truth)
metrics.frame_change: mean |grey difference| between consecutive 10 Hz frames at 64 px (128 -> 96 -> 64 BOX, channel mean: the 4A pipeline), walking only (scripted: frames of ticks 30..99; bot: ticks whose command had vx > 0.15); eis streams over pixels valid in both frames. Per run mean and median; scripted: mean over configs per segment, walking average over the 5 walking segments; bot: median of per-episode medians (4A) and mean of means
metrics.valid_fraction: eis streams: fraction of 64 px output pixels inside the wide render (a 64 px pixel is valid if its 2x2 block at 128 px is), walking ticks; also the clamp-active fraction of walking steps
metrics.phase_locked: kept = 50 Hz frames at left touchdowns (pl) or both touchdowns (pl2) during walking. (1) The sampled sequence's own wobble: std of the detrended stream angle at the kept frames, vs the same at unlocked fixed-clock samples (random start phase, 8 draws) at the kept frames' mean gap ('same rate') and at 2 Hz (every 25 steps). (2) Frame change between consecutive kept frames (gap <= 1.0 s pl / 0.6 s pl2, walking throughout) vs consecutive clock samples (same two clocks) and vs random-phase pairs with each kept pair's gap (8 per pair; phase-matched by construction at a one-stride gap, so they measure the real motion per stride). Gate row for pl_* = (1)'s locked wobble.
metrics.secondary_no_headlight: MuJoCo's headlight turns with each camera (diffuse 0.3 of the room's ~0.9): the scripted set is re-rendered with the headlight's diffuse term at 0 for every stream (10 Hz frames; wobble unaffected); frame change reported for both

aggregation: scripted: per segment the mean over the 6 configs; walking average = mean over the 5 walking segments (M3.1); turn in place reported separately. bot: wobble mean over episodes; frame change as above

gate.primary: a sensor-only stream with scripted walking-average wobble <= 2.0 deg yaw AND <= 1.0 deg pitch (the plan's 'at or below trunk level (~2 deg / 1 deg)'; the measured trunk-camera row is reported beside it, not used as a moving bar). Roll reported, not gated

not_sensor_only.trunk: a hardware change (camera moved), sim-only here; it is the 'trunk level' reference

gate.eis_usable: an eis stream counts only with walking valid-pixel fraction >= 0.95 and clamp active on <= 5% of walking steps

secondary_bars_descriptive.bot_episodes: same 2.0/1.0 deg bars on the bot episodes (realistic mix)
secondary_bars_descriptive.frame_change: <= 0.8 x the head stream's walking frame change (4A's -20% bar)
secondary_bars_descriptive.phase_locked: locked frame change <= 0.8 x the same-rate clock's; locked sequence wobble reported against both clocks

verdict_rules: eis passes (and is usable) and eis_lag or eis_lagc passes -> stage 2 = software stabilisation (rotation warp on a wide camera); no physical chicken head or learned chicken walk; next: the stage 3 representation gates on the eis stream (not run here)
eis passes but neither lag row does -> software works only with sensor-to-frame sync well under 20 ms: a hardware requirement to state
no sensor-only stream passes but the ORACLE does -> the gap is sensing or filtering: improve the estimator before any hardware
the ORACLE fails too -> rotation alone cannot reach trunk level (translation, filter limits): the trunk camera or a learned chicken walk are the remaining options
phase-locked streams that pass are a free fallback at ~1.9 Hz frames
the plan's full stage 2 gate also needs 'the stage 3 gates improve over the wobbly stream': not measured in this gate
truth_use: ORACLE stream pose; every metric (true camera orientation for wobble); bot episode success/falls for context. The eis estimate, the phase detector and the reflex read only gyro, gravity and encoders.
known_idealisations: projected gravity is exact (a real IMU's tilt is corrupted by stride accelerations)
the gyro is noise- and bias-free (FROZEN_BODY obs_noise 0)
estimate and frame are sampled at the same instant in eis (eis_lag/eis_lagc test 20 ms)
rectilinear 140 deg render stands in for a wide/fisheye lens; no motion blur, rolling shutter or exposure change
the extra renders show the state after the tick's last physics substep; the bot's own frame shows the state 5 ms earlier (identical between streams)
compute_plan: ./r8_job.sh (<= 4 processes): scripted ~15 min, bot ~12 min, no-headlight ~5 min

amendments.what: phase-locked control: a dev smoke pair (train-0001, 0.3 m/s, reflex off/on; scratch data, not a measurement room) showed that random-phase pairs with the same gap as kept pairs are one stride apart and so phase-matched by construction (locked 13.2 vs control 13.0 grey levels). Added unlocked fixed-clock controls (same rate, 2 Hz) for frame change and for the sampled sequence's wobble; the same-gap pairs are kept and relabelled. Also: eis_lagc / eis_reflex_lagc listed as sensor-only in the analysis code (they were in the protocol already).
